nodes.label: Definable
nodes.description: An object or predicate has an exact mathematical, computational, or operational definition in the current program.

nodes.label: Conditionally Definable
nodes.description: The definition is exact only after a carrier, grammar, mechanism family, history relation, observation contract, scale, target, or simulator closure is declared.

nodes.label: Empirically Identifiable
nodes.description: The available evidence resolves the declared object or target under an explicit observation and reliability contract.

nodes.label: Reportable
nodes.description: A deterministic, typed, set-valued, bounded, or target-only statement is licensed even if the full state or mechanism remains unresolved.

nodes.label: Fundamentally Undefinable
nodes.description: The requested object cannot be uniquely recovered from the stated information class; an impossibility or non-identifiability result applies.

nodes.label: Currently Undefinable
nodes.description: The program lacks a required theorem, bridge, calibration, independent validation, or measurement, without claiming principled impossibility.

nodes.label: Temporally extended ecological world
nodes.description: A possible world containing relevant history, present configuration, latent response structure, and declared counterfactual future responses.
nodes.condition: The scientifically relevant coordinates and contemplated interventions must be declared.

nodes.label: Scientific contract
nodes.description: C=(Gamma,H,Theta,D;T): future responsibilities, inherited meanings/history, retained mechanisms, evidence architecture, and report or decision target.

nodes.label: Least-information adequate state
nodes.description: The unique coarsest finite partition preserving every distinction required by a declared scientific contract on an admissible common carrier.
nodes.condition: Currently proved for declared finite exact carriers and refinement closures; no general continuous or stochastic trajectory theorem is claimed.

nodes.label: Bounded eco-genetic CREST quotient
nodes.description: A CREST-side adapter computes the coarsest adequate partition of an explicitly declared finite eco-genetic witness carrier while keeping source simulation and warning ledgers external.
nodes.condition: The aligned/anti-aligned carrier yields an exact two-block local quotient; full-domain minimality requires independently established carrier coverage.

nodes.label: Provenance-preserving research-universe registry
nodes.description: A machine-readable index of repository-owned ontology objects, contracts, claims, evidence types, non-claims, definability classes, and typed cross-repository bridges.
nodes.condition: The registry preserves source repository and snapshot boundaries and does not become the scientific evidence owner.

nodes.label: Snapshot sufficiency
nodes.description: A present snapshot is sufficient exactly when equality of snapshots implies equality of the contract-relative adequate states.
nodes.condition: Empirical identification requires a defensible map from observations to the world distinctions required by the contract.

nodes.label: Future/composition obstruction
nodes.description: A distinction compressed under a closed future grammar becomes necessary when the legal grammar is opened; exact interface memory can grow by m bits in the declared family.
nodes.condition: The small exact open interface requested may not exist; the lower bound is finite-model and grammar-relative.

nodes.label: Historical/semantic obstruction
nodes.description: A source macro-law may fail after non-nested replacement; coarsest exact repair, transport defect, route coherence, and minimum history augmentation quantify the repair.
nodes.condition: The replacement relation, histories, action grammar, and finite systems are declared rather than inferred from field data.

nodes.label: Mechanism-robust state and law
nodes.description: The coarsest observation-preserving quotient retaining only response-type distinctions that can alter declared future behavior; reports may be deterministic, typed, or set-valued.
nodes.condition: A candidate-independent deterministic law is impossible when retained response types disagree on the required transition maps.

nodes.label: Evidence licensing
nodes.description: An experiment induces compatible latent-world classes. A deterministic target is licensed exactly when it is constant on each compatible class; otherwise ambiguity must be retained.
nodes.condition: Reliability, failure architecture, calibration, target, risk, and cost must be declared.

nodes.label: Reportable target
nodes.description: A target can be deterministically reportable even when the complete adequate state is unresolved; the sharp state report can remain set-valued.

nodes.label: Monitoring-resolution debt
nodes.description: The additional finite partition resolution required for fixed evidence to identify a strengthened adequate state.

nodes.label: Restricted admissible causal hypotheses
nodes.description: The set of causal programs and parameters compatible with a declared model family, constraints, observation map, discrepancy, and tolerance.

nodes.label: Channel identifiability
nodes.description: Under positive W(z)=F(z)E(z), W-only observations cannot distinguish which factor changed; W plus one exact channel, or a stably calibrated proxy, identifies relative changes.
nodes.condition: Empirical identification requires a valid W/F/E mapping and direct or calibrated channel data.

nodes.label: Next-observation value and RACH-SEQ
nodes.description: Observation ranking that reduces the declared unresolved causal-equivalence structure without selecting a best model by fiat.
nodes.condition: Validated on controlled synthetic systems; ecological benefit requires a source-specific observation adapter and evidence contract.

nodes.label: Complete eco-genetic simulator state
nodes.description: The explicit current simulator state plus future forcing and stochastic law, which is Markov/future-sufficient under the declared closure.
nodes.condition: This is a theorem about the declared simulator representation, not natural ecological sufficiency or minimality.

nodes.label: Loss-generating eco-genetic state
nodes.description: A warning-blindly calibrated state/closure that generates the downstream functional-loss process and fixes feasibility, incidence, heterogeneity, and trajectory identity before warning inspection.

nodes.label: Conditional genetic warning
nodes.description: Baseline-relative H_alpha/H_gamma erosion preceding realized functional loss within one frozen loss-generating state.
nodes.condition: Strictly reproduced within the frozen simulator state; universal thresholds, direction-only causation, and cross-state portability remain undefined.

nodes.label: Endpoint-relevant empirical partial state
nodes.description: A synchronized measured candidate state that earns state status by held-out endpoint prediction before origin or history is tested for residual information.
nodes.condition: The proposed search basis is not assumed sufficient; natural full-state sufficiency remains open.

nodes.label: Finite world-set forecast state
nodes.description: The surviving set of declared transition worlds, their per-world support, and union/intersection projections into possible, robust, unresolved, and robustly unreachable states.
nodes.condition: Labels are conditional on the declared finite world universe and positive evidence.
